previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted for elevated amylase and lipase levels, initially without abdominal pain but with bloating and increased diarrhea. A CT scan showed no structural abnormalities in the transplanted organs, but a subsequent biopsy confirmed mild acute cellular rejection of the pancreatic transplant. She was treated with intravenous steroids and anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG), with adjustment of immunosuppressive therapy including increased tacrolimus and initiation of valganciclovir for prophylaxis. Her pancreatic enzyme levels improved significantly. Due to ATG-related leukopenia, the final dose was reduced. Blood pressure was managed with increased doxazosin, and gabapentin was restarted for phantom limb pain. She was discharged home with close follow-up, new medication instructions, and outpatient lab monitoring.

in the upper, mid and lower poles.  The resistive indices are mildly elevated

There was wall-to-wall flow with normal response to compression and

RIGHT KNEE, THREE VIEWS

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of acute fracture or malalignment.  There are

HISTORY:  ___ woman with bacteremia following pancreas transplant

History of two renal and two pancreas transplants.

COMPARISON:  ___, abdominal pelvic CT.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale, color and Doppler ultrasound was used to evaluate the
transplanted pancreas in the right lower quadrant.  The gland is normal in
echotexture, with normal vascularity.  There is no ductal dilatation or
peripancreatic fluid collection.  The splenic vein is patent.  Normal arterial
waveforms are present throughout the pancreatic parenchyma, with good
diastolic flow.

IMPRESSION:  Unremarkable appearance of the right lower quadrant transplant
pancreas without peripancreatic fluid or ductal dilatation.  Normal-appearing
pancreatic vascularity.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with diabetes mellitus, post kidney and pancreas
transplant, on chronic immunosuppression, presenting with right leg
cellulitis, worsening clinical exam.  Rule out fluid collection, soft tissue
infection, fasciitis.

COMPARISON:  Not available at the ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted sequences of the calves were
obtained prior to and following uneventful intravenous administration of
gadolinium.  Imaging was performed on a 1.5 Tesla magnet.

FINDINGS:  The patient is post left below-knee amputation, with mild soft
tissue edema adjacent to the amputation site.

The bone marrow signal is normal.  There is no evidence of osteomyelitis.

There is circumferential skin and subcutaneous edema on the right, most
pronounced in the superolateral aspect of the calf.  Mild edema is seen in the
posterior calf muscles.  The extent of edema is less pronounced, than in the
subcutaneous tissues.  There is no fluid in fascial planes.  There are no
susceptibility artifacts to suggest presence of soft tissue air.  There is no
discrete fluid collection.  The bone marrow signal is normal, there is no
evidence of osteomyelitis.

There is generalized mild muscle atrophy.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Findings in keeping with cellulitis.  Mild edema in the posterior muscle
compartment, which may be reactive, but deep soft tissue infection is not
excluded.

2.  No drainable fluid collection, fasciitis, or osteomyelitis.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT

HISTORY:  ___ woman, status post kidney and pancreatic transplant.
Recently admitted for gram-negative rod sepsis and right lower extremity
cellulitis.  IV access needed for IV antibiotics.  

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ performed the procedure
under the supervision of attending radiologist, Dr. ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access are on file.  A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire and a single lumen PICC line measuring 42 cm in length
was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the
distal SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was
confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided single lumen
PICC line placement via the right brachial venous approach.  Final internal
length is 42 cm, with the tip positioned in the distal SVC.  The line is ready
to use.
